grand_strategy.reading:
Czechia in 2026 runs two foreign policies out of one state. The government
of Andrej Babiš (ANO with the SPD and the Motorists, in office since December
2025) wants a cheaper, more domestic and more bilateral Czech Republic: no
Czech money for Ukraine, no migration pact relocation, no Green Deal, a
cautious opening to Beijing and a warm one to Jerusalem. The president, Petr
Pavel, the intelligence services and most of the arms industry keep the older
line: Russia as the threat, NATO and Berlin as the frame, Ukraine's war as
Czechia's own. Luttwak's pattern is the squeeze between them: each saving
made for the voter (the ammunition channel left unfunded, defence at 1.8%,
the opt-out from the EU loan) erodes a lever that Prague needs elsewhere -
leverage in Berlin and Washington, credibility in NATO, goodwill in Brussels
that the Dukovany loan will need before the end of 2026. What has not
changed is the structure: Russian oil and gas are out, the Korean nuclear
build is under way, Germany still takes a third of exports, and every
hostile act from Moscow (the BIS warnings, the September 2026 reciprocal
measures) pushes the cabinet back toward the line it ran against. Two signals
that are not rows: Babiš said in March 2026 that he was not planning a White
House visit and that the EU is 'always the most important'; and Pavel's
own suggestion in June 2026 that Czechia should drop the koruna for the
euro if it holds the country back, which the cabinet (which dropped the
annual euro-readiness report) will not follow.

stances.note: Russia is named the main security threat by BIS (annual report for 2025, published Aug 2026) and Prague has expelled its diplomats (18 in April 2021 over Vrbetice, Russia answered with 20 and an 'unfriendly' listing), sanctioned its influence network (Voice of Europe, 2024) and cut oil and gas imports to zero. But the grade is rival, not adversary: no Czech government has declared Russia's defeat or regime change as the aim, and the Babiš cabinet slowed the anti-Russia machinery (sanctions unit dissolved, diplomat restrictions delayed until Moscow tightened its own on 3 Sep 2026). Trend stable: hawkish state organs, softer cabinet. Bond - grievance: 1968 and Vrbetice.

stances_toward.note: The quarrel predates the war: Prague expelled 18 GRU and SVR officers over Vrbetice on 17 Apr 2021, Moscow expelled 20 and put Czechia on the 'unfriendly' list before the list existed for everyone else. Since then Czech crude and gas from Russia have gone to zero, the Voice of Europe network was sanctioned (2024), the BIS names Russia the main threat and ties the 2025 sabotage wave to 'one-time agents'; on 3 Sep 2026 Macinka summoned the ambassador over Leipzig and mirrored Moscow's restrictions on diplomats. Rival: a Babis cabinet that dissolved its sanctions unit is a government Moscow can wait out, not one it fights. Stable. Bond - grievance: 1968 on the Czech side, the 2021 expulsions as 'Russophobia' on Moscow's.

relations_from.summary: On 3 Sep 2026 Macinka summoned Russian Ambassador Ponomareva after Germany blamed Russia for the August drone attack on Leipzig/Halle airport, rejected her denial using German and Czech intelligence findings, and announced reciprocal limits for Russian diplomatic and technical staff (advance notice of travel, notes) mirroring those imposed on Czech staff in Moscow, not the strictest option under EU law.

sources.title_original: Macinka odmítl vysvětlení ruské velvyslankyně

sources.title: Macinka dissolved the ministry department that dealt with sanctions and Russian influence
sources.title_original: Macinka rozpustil ministerský odbor, který se věnoval sankcím a ruskému vlivu

relations_from.summary: At the European Council of 18-19 Dec 2025 Czechia, Hungary and Slovakia secured an exemption from financial obligations for the EUR 90bn loan to Ukraine for 2026-27 (enhanced cooperation under Article 20 TEU); the other 24 states back it with the EU budget and Babiš said Czech money must not fund it.

sources.title: EUR 90bn for Ukraine: EU summit approves exemption for Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia
EU summit decision on financing Ukraine and the Czech, Slovak and Hungarian opt-out (enhanced cooperation, Article 20 TEU)

relations_from.summary: The European Commission opened an in-depth State-aid investigation (end of 2025) into Czechia's support for two new Dukovany units (state loan of EUR 23-30bn, 40-year contract for difference, notified 2 Oct 2025); its June 2026 publication says the support may be too generous and the final decision is expected by end-2026.

sources.title: Commission raises concerns over support for new Dukovany units
KHNP says EC has dropped foreign subsidy probe into Czech project

relations_from.summary: EDF contested KHNP's win of the Dukovany tender before the Czech competition office (appeal rejected in April 2025) and the courts; a regional court blocked the planned 7 May 2025 signing until the Supreme Administrative Court lifted the injunction and the contract was signed on 4 Jun 2025.

sources.title: Czech-KHNP Dukovany contract signed after court lifts injunction
Czechs sign Dukovany nuclear deal with KHNP after court gives go-ahead

relations_from.summary: In January 2026 Ukraine's ambassador criticised Czech Speaker Okamura's New Year speech against aid to Ukraine ('Zelenskyy's junta'); Prague summoned the ambassador and Kyiv summoned the Czech chargé on 5 Jan, and on 6 Jan Sybiha and Macinka agreed by telephone to 'turn the page'; Macinka accepted an invitation to Kyiv.

sources.title: Ukraine summons Czech representative over 'shameful statements' by parliamentary speaker
Ukraine and Czechia agree to 'turn the page' after Czech speaker controversy

relations_from.summary: Defence Minister Pistorius announced an extra EUR 300m for the Czech ammunition initiative (about 50,000 long-range rounds) after meeting Defence Minister Zuna in Berlin in June 2026, lifting Germany's share past EUR 1.2bn.

sources.title: Germany adds EUR 300 million to Czech ammunition drive, about 50,000 long-range rounds for Ukraine

relations_from.summary: Babiš's first foreign visit as prime minister was to Bratislava on 8 Jan 2026, where he and Fico agreed to resume the joint government meetings; on 10 Feb he went to Vienna and then to a Slavkov-format meeting in Bratislava with Fico and Stocker.

sources.title: Prime Minister Babiš in Bratislava: we will resume the joint meetings of the Czech and Slovak governments
Prime Minister Andrej Babiš holds key talks on EU priorities in Austria and Slovakia

relations_from.summary: Babiš met Chancellor Stocker in Vienna on 10 Feb 2026 (competitiveness, energy, illegal migration); Stocker called Czechia a reliable partner and its most important trading partner in Central and Eastern Europe but said nuclear power divides them, as Austria opposes Dukovany and Temelin expansion.

sources.title: Chancellor Stocker: Czech Republic a reliable partner of Austria
sources.title_original: Bundeskanzler Stocker: Tschechische Republik als verlässlicher Partner Österreichs

sources.title: Prime Minister Andrej Babiš holds key talks on EU priorities in Austria and Slovakia

relations_from.summary: Polish President Karol Nawrocki met Babiš (leader of the election-winning ANO) in Prague on 25 Nov 2025 to discuss the next European Council and the future of the V4, alongside a meeting with President Pavel.

sources.title: Babiš and Polish president Nawrocki discuss next European Council and V4 in Prague meeting

relations_from.summary: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar met Babiš in Prague on 19 Jan 2026, called him a 'courageous and exceptional leader in Europe' and thanked Czechia as a consistent supporter; he also met Macinka and Senate President Vystrcil.

sources.title: Saar set for diplomatic visit to Czech Republic

relations_from.summary: On 12 Sep 2025 Czechia abstained (142-10-12) on the General Assembly endorsement of the New York Declaration on the two-state solution, saying Israel was not involved in drafting it, while welcoming its condemnation of 7 Oct 2023 and call for Hamas to disarm; in 2012 it was the only European state to vote against upgrading Palestine's UN status.

sources.title: Czechia's position on the UN General Assembly vote on the New York Declaration
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic

sources.title: Czechia abstains as UN endorses Israeli-Palestinian two-state resolution

relations_from.summary: In April 2026 Babiš refused a government aircraft for Senate President Vystrcil's planned trip to Taiwan, calling it part of a 'pragmatic' foreign policy that would not hurt business with China; Czech-Taiwan institutional links (direct flights from 2023, a CzechInvest office in Taipei from 2024) remain.

sources.title: Czech-Taiwan relations under Babiš: the shift is real, but shallow
Has Czechia's Taiwan policy lost its wings? Plane row signals new approach to China

relations_from.summary: Speaker Tomio Okamura made a five-day visit to China from 20 Jul 2026, the first by a senior Czech political figure since 2019; Beijing had announced in July 2025 that it would cut all contact with President Pavel after he met the Dalai Lama in India.

sources.title: Is a Czech China policy reset likely under Babiš 2.0?

relations_from.summary: Czechia and Slovakia are co-members of NATO and the EU and share gas-storage responsibility (Dolni Bojanovice) and a memorandum on enhanced cooperation of 31 Mar 2026; the Czech cabinet of Babis and the Slovak cabinet opted out together of the EU Ukraine-loan guarantees (Article 20 TEU, December 2025).
